You have to use the Chain Rule:\n$$ \\frac{d}{dx}\\ln(\\text{stuff}) \u003d \\frac{1}{\\text{stuff}} \\cdot \\text{derivative of stuff} $$\n\nMathematically, that is:\n$$ \\frac{d}{dx}\\ln(f(x)) \u003d \\frac{f\u0027(x)}{f(x)} $$\n\n**Integration is just reverse differentiation.**\nSince the derivative of $\\ln(f(x))$ is $\\frac{f\u0027(x)}{f(x)}$, it is a mathematical fact that the integral of $\\frac{f\u0027(x)}{f(x)}$ must be $\\ln(f(x))$.\n\n**You don\u0027t memorize this as a random rule.** You just recognize it: \"Oh, the top is the derivative of the bottom?
